name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:mocks → /spec:plan → /spec:run (build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:fix. Changelog (last 3): 7.282.0 — Orchestrator-only files stay out of worker waves: new optional config key orchestratorOnly (path globs) documented in the grounding contract; core.md § Read-Only Surfaces points at it; /spec:doctor check 5 warns when § Worker Rules names read-only surfaces the key does not cover. 7.281.0 — Test expiry never cuts a span it cannot bound: expire-tests --apply checks every retired case and emptied describe before cutting (ends on its own paren, closes at its opening indent, holds no foreign case or describe); an unbounded one stays in its file under a new unscannable list with one stderr line, while bounded neighbours are still cut, and a file is deleted only when no line-start case or describe is left. The test-call scanner no longer reads a JSX </ or /> as a regex, so closing and self-closing tags in .tsx tests retire cleanly instead of eating a describe's closing brace. 7.280.0 — spec-queue treats a path-shaped free-text item (a prototype contract in the plan lane) as an identity: two different paths are never near-duplicates, so prototype-driver --mark tests-derived no longer dies when another prototype's contract is pending; an identical path is still refused and groom pairs no two distinct paths.
